name: stri_subset_regex<-
title: Select Elements that Match a Given Pattern

origin.description: Replace the strings that match a regular expression.
origin.usage: stri_subset_regex(str, pattern, negate = FALSE, ..., opts_regex = NULL) <- value

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector. The result has this length.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported. The pattern vector cannot be longer than str when str is not empty.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, replace the strings that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Non-empty character vector written onto the matches, in order.

origin.details: An empty string is searched. A missing pattern keeps the original string. An empty pattern makes that element NA and warns. A missing string stays NA. value is recycled over the matches only. Named arguments are merged into opts_regex through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare list warns once the vector is known to be non-empty.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as str.
origin.example:
x <- `stri_subset_regex<-`(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "[0-9]+$", negate = TRUE, value = NA)
shown <- ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", x)
sentence <- paste0('`stri_subset_regex<-`(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "[0-9]+$", negate=TRUE, value=NA) returns ', paste(shown, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Replace the strings that match a regular expression.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, number, logical, or list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression or list of expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, replace the strings that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of regex settings.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: Further settings passed to stri_opts_regex when any are supplied.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings written onto the matches, in order. NA writes a missing value.

translation.details: Matching is stri_subset_regex. An empty string is searched. A missing pattern keeps the original string. An empty pattern makes that element NA and warns. A missing string stays NA. value is recycled over the matches only. Named arguments are merged into opts_regex through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns once the vector is known to be non-empty. The result is a new list.
translation.value: A list the same length as str.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringi.subset import stri_subset_regex_assign
x = stri_subset_regex_assign(["stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""], "[0-9]+$", negate=True, value=NA)
shown = ", ".join("NA" if item is NA else item for item in x)
print('`stri_subset_regex<-`(["stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""], "[0-9]+$", negate=True, value=NA) returns ' + shown + ".")
